headline: Small-business cash advance left owner in a seven-year fight
pages: NPR profiles Vahe Shahinian, a Los Angeles ticketing and concert promoter who took a deal in 2019 that a broker pitched as a 750,000 dollar line of credit. The catch was that he would accept a third of the sum and begin daily repayments of 3,600 dollars. He says he paid for 30, then 40, then 50 days, and the line of credit never came. For seven years he has been caught up in the merchant cash advance industry, which NPR describes as the fastest-growing source of small-business funding in the US. It is largely unregulated and costs a great deal. His lawsuit against his funders could become one of the first of its kind to go to trial. The case shows the risks for owners who turn to fast money.
